cases.deployment_evidence: The caller controls the entire URL; redirects are followed and internal hosts are reachable.
cases.prompt:
Security review of this proposed change to `webhook/checker.js`.

Deployment evidence: The caller controls the entire URL; redirects are followed and internal hosts are reachable.

```diff
diff --git a/webhook/checker.js b/webhook/checker.js
@@ -18,5 +18,6 @@
 export async function inspectWebhook(customerUrl) {
+  return fetch(customerUrl, { redirect: 'follow' });
 }
+# public endpoint; attacker controls customerUrl; internal egress is possible
```

Assess the security finding and its preconditions. Describe what the provided facts support; avoid inventing exploit evidence.
cases.chosen: Flag an SSRF path: untrusted destinations and redirects can reach internal endpoints. Constrain resolved targets at connect time and restrict redirects.
cases.rejected: There is no request-boundary risk because the first URL must use HTTPS; redirects and internal reachability do not change the security outcome.
cases.contrast_chosen: The request path accepts caller-controlled destinations and follows redirects to reachable internal services. Flag the resulting SSRF exposure and enforce boundaries.
cases.contrast_rejected: The request path chooses a fixed trusted destination and disallows redirects. The stated controls reduce this SSRF path, while DNS and egress need verification.

cases.deployment_evidence: Inputs select among fixed destinations; network and DNS enforcement remain unaudited.
cases.chosen: The described controls reduce the obvious arbitrary-destination SSRF route. Check resolution and network enforcement before claiming complete protection.
cases.rejected: All SSRF is impossible whenever a service keeps a partner allowlist. There is no reason to test destination resolution or egress bypass.
cases.contrast_chosen: The request path chooses a fixed trusted destination and disallows redirects. The stated controls reduce this SSRF path, while DNS and egress need verification.
cases.contrast_rejected: The request path accepts caller-controlled destinations and follows redirects to reachable internal services. Flag the resulting SSRF exposure and enforce boundaries.

cases.prompt:
Security review of this proposed change to `.github/workflows/pr.yml`.

Deployment evidence: pull_request_target checks out untrusted fork code and executes it with broad token authority.

```diff
diff --git a/.github/workflows/pr.yml b/.github/workflows/pr.yml
@@ -1,5 +1,9 @@
+on: pull_request_target
+permissions: write-all
+jobs:
+  run-untrusted-code:
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
+      - run: npm ci && npm test
```

Assess the security finding and its preconditions. Describe what the provided facts support; avoid inventing exploit evidence.
cases.chosen: Flag unnecessarily broad token authority for an untrusted build. Reduce to contents: read and avoid granting write scopes to the PR job.
cases.rejected: Granting write-all is a best practice because build scripts need full access to the repository by default, including write access to source.
cases.contrast_chosen: This workflow executes untrusted changes while retaining repository write authority. Flag the token privilege boundary and restrict the job before execution.
cases.contrast_rejected: This workflow tests pull requests with a read-only token and no forwarded secrets. Do not infer write-token exposure from its existence alone.

cases.deployment_evidence: The disabled certificate-verification setting is active for sensitive production requests.
cases.prompt:
Security review of this proposed change to `payments/client.js`.

Deployment evidence: The disabled certificate-verification setting is active for sensitive production requests.

```diff
diff --git a/payments/client.js b/payments/client.js
@@ -6,5 +6,6 @@
 export const paymentClient = axios.create({
+  httpsAgent: new https.Agent({ rejectUnauthorized: false }),
   baseURL: process.env.PAYMENTS_API
 });
+# service/payments/client.js is imported by deployed production checkout
```

Assess the security finding and its preconditions. Describe what the provided facts support; avoid inventing exploit evidence.
cases.chosen: Flag disabled peer-certificate rejection on production HTTPS connections. Restore certificate and hostname checks and investigate whether traffic was exposed.
cases.rejected: No TLS authenticity risk exists because encryption still occurs; ignoring certificate validation is harmless when the HTTP URL begins with https.
cases.contrast_chosen: This deployed payment client disables certificate verification for sensitive HTTPS requests. Flag a production transport-integrity risk and restore validation.
cases.contrast_rejected: This isolated local test client disables verification only for its self-signed fixture. Do not assert production impact without a deployed code path.
